subject: Azure Marketplace private offer — listing credit evidence & reseller split question
messages:
From: Rachel Myers <rachel@cloudgrid.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudGrid Procurement <procurement@cloudgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying Azure private offer listing credit and reseller split

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudGrid is close to internal approval but procurement has two outstanding items before they sign the PO:

1) The marketplace listing credit: procurement expects a documented evidence path that shows how the credit will be applied to the Azure invoice and how that maps back to our private-offer list price. We need the operational flow (invoice-to-invoice) and a sample calculation.

2) Reseller / channel split: our reseller requires a 15% netback on list price after all credits. Your private offer PDF lists a passback, but it isn't clear whether the listing credit reduces the base for reseller commission or if it sits outside that waterfall.

Can you provide a short note or sample calculation showing: final customer billed amount, marketplace listing credit, Redwood net (pre-reseller), and reseller payout? If you can include any marketplace invoice references (example line-items) that would help us get procurement unstuck.

We also need a statement on whether the listing credit is time-limited (e.g., first invoice only vs. recurring).

Appreciate quick turnaround — procurement wants to close before end of month.

Best,
Rachel

CloudGrid

Subject: Re: Clarifying Azure private offer listing credit and reseller split

Hi Rachel — thanks for laying this out clearly. Looping in Ben (channel/commissions) and Irene (marketplace ops) to make sure we give procurement both the commercial math and the invoice-level evidence.

Short answers up front:
- The listing credit is applied on the marketplace invoice as a separate line (recurring by default for the length of the private-offer term unless we explicitly mark it as one-time).
- Redwood treats the listing credit as a contra-revenue line when calculating gross-to-net for reseller commission unless the reseller contract pins commission to list price. In most marketplace reseller flows we net the credit before applying the reseller percentage.

Ben / Irene — can you confirm the sample calculation and attach a one-page invoice mock that shows the line-item mapping? Also attaching the SOW Rachel sent.

Ava

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarifying Azure private offer listing credit and reseller split

Hey team — quick math and a couple of scenarios. I pulled the channel template and a sample waterfall. See the attached workback.

Scenario A (listing credit nets before reseller):
- List price (monthly): $100,000
- Marketplace listing credit (recurring): $20,000
- Redwood net recognized: $80,000
- Reseller payout @15% of Redwood net: $12,000
- Customer billed (Azure invoice): $80,000 after credit line applied

Scenario B (listing credit treated as outside the commission base):
- List price (monthly): $100,000
- Redwood recognizes $100,000, marketplace shows a separate credit to customer -$20,000
- Reseller payout @15% of list price: $15,000
- Net to Redwood after reseller: $85,000
- Customer billed: $80,000 (same end-customer cost) but accounting treatment differs for reseller payout and tax handling.

Notes:
- Azure typically exposes the credit as a line-level discount on the invoice. That means accounting teams often record the contra-revenue and compute commission on net revenue (Scenario A). If CloudGrid's reseller contract explicitly requires commission on gross/list, we can honor that (Scenario B) but procurement needs to sign off because it changes the reseller economics.
- Tax & VAT handling varies by jurisdiction; the reseller payout base can have tax implications.

I'm attaching channel_margin_workback.xlsx with the two scenarios and a mock marketplace invoice (example lines). Irene — can you produce the one-page evidence file with actual marketplace SKU names and where the credit appears? Rachel, if CloudGrid wants the credit to be one-time we can make it happen but need to reflect that in the PO language.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Channel GTM, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: channel_margin_workback.xlsx]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Hi Rachel — attached is a one-page marketplace invoice mock and a short note on operational flow. Key points:

- Evidence path: Azure marketplace will issue a monthly invoice to CloudGrid with line items. The listing credit appears as a separate negative line: 
  - SKU: REDWOOD-INF-INFERENCE
  - Description: Private offer listing credit (recurring)
  - Amount: -$20,000

- Accounting mapping: Our finance team records the credit as contra-revenue; the marketplace invoice reference (invoice ID) is stored in our deal record and shared with partners for reconciliation.

- Payout timing: reseller payments are calculated monthly based on the revenue recorded in Redwood's GL. If you want reseller payout based on list price instead of net, we will need a procurement note in the PO and a short amendment to the reseller agreement to avoid disputes.

- Sample attachments included: marketplace_invoice_mock.pdf (shows how line appears), channel_margin_workback.xlsx (Ben's), and a short operations runbook link for reconciliation.

Irene
